text:
Anna: Quick sync — we need to lock the barrier remediation table and concrete thresholds for go/no-go. Focus areas: SLA, docs, support, monitoring, pricing. What's a realistic set of acceptance metrics and who owns remediation?
Mike: Perf test note: hosted API 95th latency with long-context prompts is at ~180ms, target is 120ms. If we can't get under 140ms in the next 48h we should enable model fallback.
Jordan: Telemetry + alerts: agreed we need both relative and absolute triggers. My proposal: alert if `error_rate > 0.5%` sustained for 5m OR `p50_latency > 200ms` and `p95_latency > 500ms` for 3m. Critical page if either `5xx_rate > 1%` or `request_drop_rate > 0.5%` for 2m.
Sarah: Docs/runbooks: must include exact rollback commands, escalation matrix, and customer comms templates. I'll add the commands for fallback & circuit-breaker. Example:
```
# emergency fallback to quantized variant
redwood deploy --model rdx-model-v2-q --route default --reason "perf-regression-goal:ga"
# enable circuit breaker for spiky traffic
redwood api-config set --route default --circuit_breaker 0.02
```
Mike: For rollback triggers I'd like a simple boolean checklist that can be evaluated in shiproom:
- sustained p95 > 300ms for 10m?
- 5xx spike > 2x baseline for 5m?
- billing unit cost > 120% of expected for 2 hours?
If >=2 true -> initiate fallback.
Anna: Good. Let's make the shipping decision matrix explicit in the playbook. Owner: @Mike for performance fixes, @Jordan for alerts/telemetry, @Sarah for runbooks & comms. Deadline: EOD +2 (48h).
Jordan: Alert rule yaml (templated) below — we'll wire to pager and slack ops channel: 
```
alert: high-5xx-spike
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",route="default"}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="default"}[1m])) > 0.01
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: critical
annotations:
  summary: "High 5xx rate on default route"
  runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/5xx-spike"
```
ops-bot: Scheduled canary metrics snapshot uploaded: https://metrics.redwood/internal/canary/1717504321 (canary window: 30m) :white_check_mark:
Sarah: Customer-facing pricing/backstop note — product team OK to gate launch on a billing backstop: if projected unit cost exceeds forecast by >20% for 6h, finance wants an automatic throttling policy and sales notification template. I'll draft the template.
Mike: Actionable remediation steps for perf: 1) tune batching config (owner: eng-runtime), 2) enable prefix KV caching for common prompts (owner: inference), 3) temp autoscale bump (owner: eng-infra). I'll open PRs and tag owners.
Anna: Final checklist for go/no-go (proposal):
- SLA targets certified by SRE and Eng: p99 latency < X, error rate < Y (owner: Mike)
- Runbooks and comms ready (owner: Sarah)
- Monitoring & alert thresholds in prod (owner: Jordan)
- Billing guardrails & throttling policy (owner: Sarah + Finance)
- Rollback/fallback commands validated in staging (owner: Mike)
If all owners sign off by EOD +2 -> greenlight. If any critical trigger fires during burn-in -> pause rollout and execute fallback.
Jordan: I'll push rules to staging tomorrow and start synthetic checks against canary.
Sarah: I'll assemble the comms + support playbook and post to #product-ops before EOD +1.
Mike: I'll benchmark the quantized fallback and surface expected perf/cost delta in the PR.
Anna: Ok — thanks. @everyone please react with :thumbsup: when you accept owners & deadlines, or :eyes: if you need to renegotiate. We'll reconvene in 24h if anything changes.
